**Order filled:** bought 20 AAPL at $221.60 (limit), $4,432 notional — well inside the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, funded from the $50,000 cash balance (no funds left the account), leaving 100 MSFT shares untouched.

**Summary:** AAPL was the only eligible name with a clean setup this morning. The feed showed 27 minutes of quiet drift from 221.84 down to 220.53 (−0.6%) on nothing but repeated, recycled "shares little changed"/"supplier builds steady" headlines and unchanged analyst estimates — noise rather than a catalyst, so a lower entry looked reasonable rather than a falling knife. The one thing that gave me pause was a genuine data conflict: the broker's quote read 222.70 (confirmed twice, as of 15:05Z) versus the feed's last prints near 220.5 at 09:57, i.e. ~1% apart with no headline to explain it. Because the mandate requires limit prices close to the current market price, I refused to anchor to one ambiguous print and instead set the limit at 221.60 — roughly 0.5% from either candidate price — which fills at or below the prevailing price under either interpretation and never overpays; it filled at 221.60 for 20 shares. On fundamentals I went in small, supported by Apple's fiscal 2024 results as I recall them from memory (not re-verified against the 10-K in this session): diluted EPS of $6.08, revenue of $391.0B, net income of $93.7B and operating cash flow of $118.3B — a business generating about $118B of cash on $391B of sales at a ~24% net margin, which is why I was content to hold a modest starter position through an oddly-quoted morning. I'd flag one open item for you: the feed-versus-broker price gap should be reconciled with your data provider before adding further AAPL exposure today, and I have ~$15,568 of the $20,000 daily budget still available if you want to add on a confirmed quote.
